```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

from pcntoolkit import (
    BLR,
    BsplineBasisFunction,
    NormativeModel,
    NormData,
    plot_qq
)

import pcntoolkit.util.output


# ============================================================
# PATHS
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# PATHS
# ============================================================

current_dir = Path.cwd().parent

input_path = current_dir / "results" / "combined_dataset" / "Model_dataframe.csv"

model_dir = current_dir / "results" / "normative_model"

model_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


# ============================================================
# LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

model_df = pd.read_csv(input_path)

pcntoolkit.util.output.Output.set_show_messages(False)


# ============================================================
# DEFINE MODEL VARIABLES
# ============================================================

response_vars = [f"comp{i}" for i in range(1, 19)]

batch_effects = []

covariates = [
    col for col in model_df.columns
    if col not in (
        [
            "Scan_id",
            "Participant_Id",
            "Session",
            "Dataset_name"
        ]
        + response_vars
    )
]


# ============================================================
# CHECK MODEL SETUP
# ============================================================
print("\nRows:")
print(len(model_df))

print("\nResponses:")
print(response_vars)

print("\nCovariates:")
print(covariates)

print("\nBatch effects:")
print(batch_effects)

print(
    "\nMissing covariate values:",
    model_df[covariates]
    .isna()
    .sum()
    .sum()
)

print(
    "Missing response values:",
    model_df[response_vars]
    .isna()
    .sum()
    .sum()
)


# ============================================================
# CREATE NORMDATA
# ============================================================

norm_data = NormData.from_dataframe(
    name="DigitalRodent",
    dataframe=model_df,
    covariates=covariates,
    batch_effects=batch_effects,
    response_vars=response_vars,
    remove_Nan=False
)


# ============================================================
# TRAIN / TEST SPLIT
# ============================================================

train, test = norm_data.train_test_split()


# ============================================================
# BLR MODEL
# ============================================================

# Non-linear age effect: B-spline basis on Age only.
# Without a basis function BLR is linear in every covariate,
# which is why the centile curves came out as straight lines.
# The other covariates (scanner, sex, anesthesia, ...) stay linear.
age_column = covariates.index("Age(week)")

model = NormativeModel(
    BLR(
        basis_function_mean=BsplineBasisFunction(
            basis_column=[age_column],
            degree=3,
            nknots=5
        ),
        basis_function_var=BsplineBasisFunction(
            basis_column=[age_column],
            degree=3,
            nknots=5
        ),
        heteroskedastic=True
    ),
    inscaler="standardize",
    outscaler="standardize",
    savemodel=True,
    evaluate_model=True,
    saveresults=True,
    saveplots=True,
    save_dir=str(model_dir)
)


# ============================================================
# FIT MODEL
# ============================================================

model.fit_predict(
    train,
    test
)


# ============================================================
# QQ PLOTS
# ============================================================

qq_dir = (
    model_dir
    / "plots"
    / "qq"
)

qq_dir.mkdir(
    parents=True,
    exist_ok=True
)

plot_qq(
    test,
    plot_id_line=True,
    save_dir=str(qq_dir)
)


# ============================================================
# RESULTS
# ============================================================

train_stats = train.get_statistics_df()
test_stats = test.get_statistics_df()

print("\nTrain statistics:")
display(train_stats)

print("\nTest statistics:")
display(test_stats)

train_stats.to_csv(
    model_dir
    / "Train_statistics.csv",
    index=False
)

test_stats.to_csv(
    model_dir
    / "Test_statistics.csv",
    index=False
)


# ============================================================
# DONE
# ============================================================

print("\nBLR training finished.")

print("\nSaved to:")
print(model_dir)

```
